prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct Tally and rejects broken ones. This one holds state, so the ORDER of your calls matters. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Testing an object is not like testing a function: the same call can give different answers depending on what happened before it, so the sequence is part of the test. total() called twice in a row must give the same answer both times -- that single repeated call is the only thing that catches an implementation which drains the tally as a side effect, and it is the kind of bug that survives every test suite written as one call per line. Checking the total after reset(), and again after adding to a freshly reset tally, is what proves reset actually did something rather than being an empty method.
hints: Call total() twice in a row without adding anything in between. The answer must be the same both times.
After reset(), add something and check the new total: an empty reset() looks correct if you only ever check it once at the end.
The contract allows negative numbers, so add(-2) and confirm the total went DOWN.
